title: Stream boundary heartbeats and sanitization for interleaved tool/function calls
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: When a response is streamed and interleaves tool/function calls, we currently lack consistent per-chunk metrics and trace anchor points that reliably map emitted tokens to a specific call boundary. This prevents accurate SLOing, makes billing attribution fuzzy, and increases risk of PII leakage in logs. We also need a backward-compatible behavior for older SDK clients that don't understand new stream markers.

Goal: Add a lightweight, standardized set of Stream Events (heartbeat + boundary markers) and per-chunk telemetry fields, wire these into trace spans (one span per logical stream +- explicit subspans for tool calls), and ensure all streaming logs/metrics pass through a sanitization/redaction pipeline before leaving the host. Maintain a compatibility shim for legacy clients.

Scope: server runtime + streaming API surface + SDK compatibility headers + observability dashboards and alert rules. Not part of this ticket: UI dashboard redesign (separate PM ticket), long-term analytics storage migration.

Why now: Several customer incidents and internal root-cause analyses found mis-attributed token spikes and PII appearance in debug logs during tool call output. Incremental delivery is safe and unblockable for Dedicated/private deployments first.
acceptance_criteria: Stream events include HEARTBEAT, PARTIAL_OUTPUT, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_END, FINAL_CHUNK and are produced for every streamed response
Per-chunk telemetry emitted: chunk_latency_ms, tokens_emitted, kv_cache_hits, call_boundary_tag (none | tool:<name>)
Tracing: top-level stream span created per request; TOOL_CALL_* events create child spans that are linked to chunk metrics via span_id header
All streamed log lines pass through redaction pipeline before write: PII token scrub rules applied and redaction markers included in traces
Legacy SDKs receive compatible fallbacks via X-Stream-Compat header: they get the same tokens but without structured markers and a sideband non-blocking event webhook for tooling
Unit + integration tests validate sampling, redaction, and span-linking for toolcall interleaving; e2e load test shows <2% p99 amplification in emitter-side CPU
Dashboard widgets updated: per-stream latency histogram, per-tool-call token distribution, and redaction-rate gauge
comments: 2025-02-25 Ava Patel: Raised initial problem after postmortem for INC-2025-02 where tool-call tokens were misattributed and PII leaked to debug logs. Drafted goals and scope.

2025-02-27 Diego Morales: Added implementation plan — runtime will emit JSON-framed sideband events in the stream prefix so existing streaming consumers can ignore unknown frames. See design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/STREAMBOUND+Observability+Design

2025-02-28 PR feedback by Priya Singh: asked for explicit schema for per-chunk telemetry and proposed namespacing to avoid collisions with existing metrics. Suggest names: rwi.chunk.latency_ms, rwi.chunk.tokens, rwi.chunk.kv_hits, rwi.chunk.call_boundary

2025-03-01 Engineering note by Diego Morales: Implemented prototype in runtime that injects <EVENT> JSON frames with type field. Preliminary benchmark: 5% CPU overhead at median request size, 1.6x memory for buffer windows. Link to prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5873

2025-03-02 Security review request by Ava Patel: requested security_review_required=true and attached redaction rules. See policy snapshot: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/STREAM+Redaction+Rules

2025-03-03 QA report by Lina Chen: sanity tests pass for happy path; discovered edge-case where TOOL_CALL_END may arrive in same chunk as FINAL_CHUNK — added test and clarified ordering semantics in ACs

2025-03-04 Diego Morales: Marking In Progress. Next steps: land runtime PR, add SDK compatibility header handling, add trace span exporter update, and schedule internal canary for Dedicated customers. Planned rollout window: 2025-03-11 to 2025-03-13 (canary) then 2025-03-18 global ramp

Reviewer notes (2025-03-04) by Priya Singh: Ensure redaction pipeline emits a boolean 'redacted' flag for post-hoc audits; add metric rwi.redaction.rate per-stream so we can alert on sudden increases.
